-- | Spectra's pure lowering from presentation values to Typst documents.
--
-- Generic syntax construction and escaping belong to the independent `Typst`
-- package. This module contains only presentation-specific mapping decisions.

import Data.List (append)

import Data.String (contains)

import Typst as T

import Layout (..)

import Theme (Theme, prism_theme)

pub type TypstDocument = TypstDocument {
  format: String,
  source: String,
  logical_slides: Int,
  physical_pages: Int,
  assets: List(String)
} deriving (Eq, Show)

fn color(name : String, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  let value =
    if name == "" then
      theme.foreground
    elif name == "accent" then
      theme.accent
    elif name == "muted" then
      theme.muted
    else
      name
  T.call("rgb", [T.string("#{value}")])

fn alignment(align : Align) : T.Doc =
  match align of
    Left => T.atom("left")
    Center => T.atom("center")
    Right => T.atom("right")

fn inline_doc(x : Inline, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match x of
    Plain(s) => T.call("text", [T.string(s)])
    InlineCode(s) =>
      T.call("raw", [T.string(s), T.named("lang", T.string("prism"))])
    Emphasis(xs) => T.content_call("emph", Nil, inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Strong(xs) => T.content_call("strong", Nil, inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Link(url, xs) =>
      T.content_call("link", [T.string(url)], inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Colored(name, xs) =>
      T.content_call(
          "text",
          [T.named("fill", color(name, theme))],
          inline_docs(xs, theme),
        )

fn inline_docs(xs : List(Inline), theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match xs of
    Nil => T.empty()
    Cons(x, Nil) => inline_doc(x, theme)
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      T.concat_docs([
          inline_doc(x, theme),
          T.atom(" + "),
          inline_docs(rest, theme),
        ])

fn max2(a : Int, b : Int) : Int =
  if a > b then
    a
  else
    b

fn max_stage_list(xs : List(Pict)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(p, rest) => max2(max_stage(p), max_stage_list(rest))

-- | Highest reveal stage mentioned by a pict tree.
pub fn max_stage(p : Pict) : Int =
  match p of
    Empty => 0
    Text(_, _) => 0
    CodeBlock(_, _) => 0
    Image(_) => 0
    Rectangle(_, _, _) => 0
    Row(_, xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Column(_, _, xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Overlay(xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Inset(_, _, _, _, child) => max_stage(child)
    Fit(_, child) => max_stage(child)
    Fragment(stage, child) => max2(stage, max_stage(child))
    RawTypst(_) => 0

fn assets_list(xs : List(Pict)) : List(String) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(p, rest) => append(pict_assets(p), assets_list(rest))

-- | Logical, project-relative asset names reached by a pict tree.
pub fn pict_assets(p : Pict) : List(String) =
  match p of
    Empty => Nil
    Text(_, _) => Nil
    CodeBlock(_, _) => Nil
    Image(path) => [path]
    Rectangle(_, _, _) => Nil
    Row(_, xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Column(_, _, xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Overlay(xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Inset(_, _, _, _, child) => pict_assets(child)
    Fit(_, child) => pict_assets(child)
    Fragment(_, child) => pict_assets(child)
    RawTypst(_) => Nil

fn pict_docs(xs : List(Pict), stage : Int, theme : Theme) : List(T.Doc) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(p, rest) =>
      Cons(pict_doc(p, stage, theme), pict_docs(rest, stage, theme))

fn pict_doc(p : Pict, stage : Int, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match p of
    Empty => T.atom("none")
    Text(style, xs) =>
      let size =
        if style.size <= 0 then
          theme.body_size
        else
          style.size
      T.call("align", [
          alignment(style.align),
          T.content_call(
              "text",
              [
                  T.named("size", T.pt(size)),
                  T.named("fill", color(style.color, theme)),
                ],
              inline_docs(xs, theme),
            ),
        ])
    CodeBlock(language, source) =>
      T.content_call("block", [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("fill", color(theme.code_background, theme)), T.named("inset", T.pt(14)), T.named("radius", T.pt(7))], T.content_call("text", [T.named("fill", color(theme.code_foreground, theme)), T.named("font", T.string(theme.code_font)), T.named("size", T.pt(theme.code_size))], T.call("raw", [
          T.string(source),
          T.named("block", T.atom("true")),
          T.named("lang", T.string(language)),
        ])))
    Image(path) =>
      T.call("image", [
          T.string(path),
          T.named("width", T.percent(100)),
          T.named("height", T.percent(100)),
          T.named("fit", T.string("contain")),
        ])
    Rectangle(name, width, height) =>
      T.call("rect", [
          T.named("width", T.pt(width)),
          T.named("height", T.pt(height)),
          T.named("fill", color(name, theme)),
        ])
    Row(gap, children) =>
      T.call(
          "stack",
          Cons(
              T.named("dir", T.atom("ltr")),
              Cons(
                  T.named("spacing", T.pt(gap)),
                  pict_docs(children, stage, theme),
                ),
            ),
        )
    Column(gap, align, children) =>
      T.call("align", [
          alignment(align),
          T.call(
              "stack",
              Cons(
                  T.named("dir", T.atom("ttb")),
                  Cons(
                      T.named("spacing", T.pt(gap)),
                      pict_docs(children, stage, theme),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        ])
    Overlay(children) =>
      T.content_call(
          "block",
          [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("height", T.percent(100))],
          T.call("stack", pict_docs(children, stage, theme)),
        )
    Inset(top, right, bottom, left, child) =>
      T.content_call(
          "block",
          [
              T.named("inset", T.tuple([
                  T.named("top", T.pt(top)),
                  T.named("right", T.pt(right)),
                  T.named("bottom", T.pt(bottom)),
                  T.named("left", T.pt(left)),
                ])),
            ],
          pict_doc(child, stage, theme),
        )
    Fit(_, child) =>
      T.content_call(
          "box",
          [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("height", T.percent(100))],
          pict_doc(child, stage, theme),
        )
    Fragment(at, child) =>
      if at <= stage then
        pict_doc(child, stage, theme)
      else
        T.atom("none")
    RawTypst(source) => T.raw(source)

-- | Render a pict for one concrete reveal stage.
pub fn render_pict(p : Pict, stage : Int, theme : Theme) : String =
  T.render(96, pict_doc(p, stage, theme))

fn title_doc(title : Option(String)) : T.Doc =
  match title of
    None => T.atom("none")
    Some(value) => T.string(value)

-- | Render one physical page from a logical slide and reveal stage.
pub fn render_slide_page(
  title : Option(String),
  body : Pict,
  stage : Int,
  theme : Theme
) : String =
  T.render(96, T.code(T.call("spectra-slide", [
      title_doc(title),
      pict_doc(body, stage, theme),
    ])))

-- | The small presentation runtime prepended to every generated document.
pub fn typst_prelude(theme : Theme) : String =
  T.document([
      T.atom("// Generated by Spectra. Inspect, diff, and keep this artifact."),
      T.set_rule("document", [T.named("date", T.atom("none"))]),
      T.set_rule("page", [
          T.named("width", T.atom("13.333in")),
          T.named("height", T.atom("7.5in")),
          T.named("margin", T.pt(theme.margin_pt)),
          T.named("fill", color(theme.background, theme)),
        ]),
      T.set_rule("text", [
          T.named("font", T.string(theme.text_font)),
          T.named("size", T.pt(theme.body_size)),
          T.named("fill", color(theme.foreground, theme)),
        ]),
      T.set_rule("par", [T.named("leading", T.atom("0.65em"))]),
      T.let_function("spectra-slide", [T.atom("title"), T.atom("body")], [
          T.call("rect", [
              T.named("width", T.percent(100)),
              T.named("height", T.pt(2)),
              T.named("fill", color("accent", theme)),
            ]),
          T.call("v", [T.pt(16)]),
          T.concat_docs([
              T.atom("set "),
              T.call("align", [T.atom("left + top")]),
            ]),
          T.if_suite("title != none", [
              T.content_call(
                  "text",
                  [
                      T.named("size", T.pt(theme.title_size)),
                      T.named("weight", T.atom("700")),
                      T.named("fill", color(theme.accent, theme)),
                    ],
                  T.atom("title"),
                ),
              T.call("v", [T.pt(18)]),
            ]),
          T.atom("body"),
        ]),
      T.empty(),
    ])

test fn prelude_disables_ambient_pdf_dates() =
  if (contains("#set document(date: none)", typst_prelude(prism_theme))) then
    ()
  else
    fail()

-- | Code-oriented Spectra combinators.

import Layout (Pict, Inline, CodeBlock, InlineCode)

-- | A fenced source block. The language name is passed to Typst's raw-text
-- renderer, which can apply syntax highlighting when it knows the language.
pub fn code_block(language : String, source : String) : Pict =
  CodeBlock(language, source)

-- | A Prism source block.
pub fn prism_code(source : String) : Pict = code_block("prism", source)

-- | Inline monospace source.
pub fn inline_code(source : String) : Inline = InlineCode(source)

Doctests on slides: the examples a reflected declaration carries.

`reflect fn f` hands back a declaration as the formatter prints it, comment block included, so a docstring's fenced examples arrive with it. Taking them back apart is all a slide needs in order to show an example beside the output that example produces.

The fences are the ones the compiler's own doctest runner reads: a `prism` fence is the example, and an `output` fence opening on the line right after it is what running the example prints. The adjacency is the runner's rule, kept here for a reason: an output block it would not pair up is one nothing checks, so a slide must not show it. Nothing here runs anything, so a deck stays a pure value. `spectra build` shells out to that runner instead, which is what makes the outputs printed on the slides the outputs the code actually produces. An example that defines `main` runs as a whole program and one that does not runs as a prompt line, exactly as in generated documentation.

A line marked as hidden compiles for the runner but stays off the slide, so setup a reader does not need never reaches the screen.

-- | Doctests on slides: the examples a reflected declaration carries.
--
-- `reflect fn f` hands back a declaration as the formatter prints it, comment
-- block included, so a docstring's fenced examples arrive with it. Taking them
-- back apart is all a slide needs in order to show an example beside the output
-- that example produces.
--
-- The fences are the ones the compiler's own doctest runner reads: a `prism`
-- fence is the example, and an `output` fence opening on the line right after
-- it is what running the example prints. The adjacency is the runner's rule,
-- kept here for a reason: an output block it would not pair up is one nothing
-- checks, so a slide must not show it. Nothing here runs anything, so a deck
-- stays a pure value.
-- `spectra build` shells out to that runner instead, which is what makes the
-- outputs printed on the slides the outputs the code actually produces. An
-- example that defines `main` runs as a whole program and one that does not
-- runs as a prompt line, exactly as in generated documentation.
--
-- A line marked as hidden compiles for the runner but stays off the slide, so
-- setup a reader does not need never reaches the screen.

import Layout (Pict, column)

import Code (code_block, prism_code)

import Data.String (contains, lines_of, split, starts_with, trim)

import Data.List (map, reverse)

-- | One fenced example: the source a slide shows, and the output the doctest
-- runner proves it prints (empty when the docstring pins none).
pub type Example = Example { code: String, output: String } deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | A reflected declaration taken apart: the prose of its docstring, the
-- examples that docstring fences, and the declaration itself.
pub type Doc = Doc {
  prose: String,
  examples: List(Example),
  definition: String
} deriving (Eq, Show)

-- Which part of a docstring the walk is inside. A fence the runner does not
-- read (`text`, `console`) is still a fence, and its contents are neither prose
-- nor an example.
type Region
  = InProse
  | InCode
  | InOutput
  | InOther

let doc_marker : String = "-- | "

let doc_marker_bare : String = "-- |"

let comment_marker : String = "-- "

let comment_bare : String = "--"

let fence : String = "```"

let prism_fence : String = "```prism"

let output_fence : String = "```output"

-- The runner's hidden-line marker: the line compiles but is not shown.
let hidden_marker : String = "#"

-- Output is shown verbatim, with no language for a highlighter to guess at.
let output_language : String = "text"

let newline : Int = char_at("\n", 0)

fn drop_prefix(prefix : String, line : String) : String =
  substring(line, str_len(prefix), str_len(line) - str_len(prefix))

-- One comment line as its author wrote it, marker removed.
fn strip_marker(line : String) : String =
  if starts_with(doc_marker, line) then
    drop_prefix(doc_marker, line)
  elif starts_with(doc_marker_bare, line) then
    drop_prefix(doc_marker_bare, line)
  elif starts_with(comment_marker, line) then
    drop_prefix(comment_marker, line)
  elif line == comment_bare then
    ""
  else
    line

-- An output fence is reached only by the code fence above it, never from prose:
-- the runner pairs the two by adjacency, so a detached output block is one
-- nothing checks, and a slide must not show it as though something did.
fn region_of(line : String) : Option(Region) =
  if starts_with(prism_fence, line) then
    Some(InCode)
  elif starts_with(fence, line) then
    Some(InOther)
  else
    None

fn closes(line : String) : Bool = trim(line) == fence

fn hidden(line : String) : Bool =
  line == hidden_marker || starts_with("{hidden_marker} ", line)

-- The comment block a declaration leads with, and the declaration itself. The
-- block ends at the first line that is not a comment, so a comment inside the
-- body stays part of the body.
fn split_comment(
  lines : List(String),
  doc : List(String)
) : (List(String), List(String)) =
  match lines of
    Nil => (reverse(doc), Nil)
    Cons(line, rest) =>
      if starts_with(comment_bare, line) then
        split_comment(rest, Cons(line, doc))
      else
        (reverse(doc), lines)

-- An output fence answers the example just above it, which is the one most
-- recently pushed.
fn with_output(text : String, acc : List(Example)) : List(Example) =
  match acc of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(e, rest) => Cons(Example { code = e.code, output = text }, rest)

-- Where to resume after a code fence closes: inside the output block when one
-- opens on the very next line, in prose otherwise.
fn after_code(
  rest : List(String),
  prose : List(String),
  acc : List(Example)
) : (List(String), List(Example)) =
  match rest of
    Cons(next, tail) =>
      if starts_with(output_fence, next) then
        walk(tail, InOutput, Nil, prose, acc)
      else
        walk(rest, InProse, Nil, prose, acc)
    Nil => (reverse(prose), reverse(acc))

fn walk(
  lines : List(String),
  region : Region,
  buf : List(String),
  prose : List(String),
  acc : List(Example)
) : (List(String), List(Example)) =
  match lines of
    Nil => (reverse(prose), reverse(acc))
    Cons(line, rest) =>
      match region of
        InProse =>
          match region_of(line) of
            Some(next) => walk(rest, next, Nil, prose, acc)
            None => walk(rest, InProse, Nil, Cons(line, prose), acc)
        InCode =>
          if closes(line) then
            after_code(
                rest,
                prose,
                Cons(
                    Example { code = lines_of(reverse(buf)), output = "" },
                    acc,
                  ),
              )
          elif hidden(line) then
            walk(rest, InCode, buf, prose, acc)
          else
            walk(rest, InCode, Cons(line, buf), prose, acc)
        InOutput =>
          if closes(line) then
            walk(
                rest,
                InProse,
                Nil,
                prose,
                with_output(lines_of(reverse(buf)), acc),
              )
          else
            walk(rest, InOutput, Cons(line, buf), prose, acc)
        InOther =>
          if closes(line) then
            walk(rest, InProse, Nil, prose, acc)
          else
            walk(rest, InOther, buf, prose, acc)

-- | Take a reflected declaration apart into prose, examples, and the
-- declaration itself.
pub fn read_doc(reflected : String) : Doc =
  let (comment, body) = split_comment(split(newline, reflected), Nil)
  let (prose, examples) =
    walk(map(strip_marker, comment), InProse, Nil, Nil, Nil)
  Doc {
    prose = lines_of(prose),
    examples = examples,
    definition = lines_of(body)
  }

-- | The examples a reflected declaration's docstring fences.
pub fn examples_of(reflected : String) : List(Example) =
  read_doc(reflected).examples

-- | One example as its source over the output it prints.
pub fn example_pict(e : Example) : Pict =
  if e.output == "" then
    prism_code(e.code)
  else
    column(10, [prism_code(e.code), code_block(output_language, e.output)])

-- | Every example a reflected declaration carries, stacked.
pub fn doctest(reflected : String) : Pict =
  column(18, map(example_pict, examples_of(reflected)))

-- | A reflected declaration without its comment block, as a source block. This
-- is the code a docstring documents, with the documentation left behind.
pub fn definition(reflected : String) : Pict =
  prism_code(read_doc(reflected).definition)

test fn a_docstring_yields_its_example_and_output() =
  let src = r"""
    -- | Twice.
    -- ```prism
    -- double(21)
    -- ```
    -- ```output
    -- 42
    -- ```
    fn double(x : Int) : Int = x * 2
    """
  let doc = read_doc(src)
  match doc.examples of
    Cons(e, Nil) =>
      if (e.code == "double(21)" && e.output == "42" && doc.prose == "Twice.") then
        ()
      else
        fail()
    _ => fail()

test fn a_hidden_line_stays_out_of_the_shown_example() =
  let src = r"""
    -- | Setup.
    -- ```prism
    -- # let n = 21
    -- double(n)
    -- ```
    fn double(x : Int) : Int = x * 2
    """
  let doc = read_doc(src)
  match doc.examples of
    Cons(e, Nil) =>
      if e.code == "double(n)" && e.output == "" then
        ()
      else
        fail()
    _ => fail()

test fn the_definition_survives_without_its_comment_block() =
  let src = r"""
    -- | Twice.
    fn double(x : Int) : Int = x * 2
    """
  let doc = read_doc(src)
  if doc.definition == "fn double(x : Int) : Int = x * 2" then
    ()
  else
    fail()

-- The runner pairs an output block with the example directly above it, so one
-- separated by a blank line is checked by nothing and shown by nothing.
test fn a_detached_output_block_is_not_attached() =
  let src = r"""
    -- | Twice.
    -- ```prism
    -- double(21)
    -- ```
    --
    -- ```output
    -- 99
    -- ```
    fn double(x : Int) : Int = x * 2
    """
  let doc = read_doc(src)
  match doc.examples of
    Cons(e, Nil) =>
      if e.output == "" && not(contains("99", doc.prose)) then
        ()
      else
        fail()
    _ => fail()

test fn a_declaration_with_no_docstring_has_no_examples() =
  match read_doc("type Light = Red | Amber | Green").examples of
    Nil => ()
    _ => fail()

-- | Backend-neutral layout values for Spectra.
--
-- These constructors describe intent. They deliberately contain no measured
-- coordinates or Typst-specific layout state.

pub type Align = Left | Center | Right deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type FitMode = Contain | Cover deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type Inline
  = Plain(String)
  | Emphasis(List(Inline))
  | Strong(List(Inline))
  | InlineCode(String)
  | Link(String, List(Inline))
  | Colored(String, List(Inline))
  deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type TextStyle = TextStyle {
  size: Int,
  color: String,
  align: Align
} deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type Pict
  = Empty
  | Text(TextStyle, List(Inline))
  | CodeBlock(String, String)
  | Image(String)
  | Rectangle(String, Int, Int)
  | Row(Int, List(Pict))
  | Column(Int, Align, List(Pict))
  | Overlay(List(Pict))
  | Inset(Int, Int, Int, Int, Pict)
  | Fit(FitMode, Pict)
  | Fragment(Int, Pict)
  | RawTypst(String)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | Normal body text in the theme foreground. A size of zero means "theme
-- body size" to the renderer.
pub fn text(s : String) : Pict =
  Text(TextStyle { size = 0, color = "", align = Left }, [Plain(s)])

-- | Rich inline text in the theme foreground.
pub fn rich_text(xs : List(Inline)) : Pict =
  Text(TextStyle { size = 0, color = "", align = Left }, xs)

-- | A paragraph-sized inline sequence. This is an authoring synonym for
-- `rich_text`, retained because it reads naturally inside a slide builder.
pub fn para(xs : List(Inline)) : Pict = rich_text(xs)

-- | A bullet item rendered as an accent arrow and rich inline text.
pub fn item_text(xs : List(Inline)) : Pict =
  rich_text(Cons(Colored("accent", [Plain("→ ")]), xs))

-- | A plain bullet item.
pub fn item(s : String) : Pict = item_text([Plain(s)])

pub fn row(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict = Row(gap, children)

pub fn column(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict = Column(gap, Left, children)

pub fn centered(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict =
  Column(gap, Center, children)

pub fn overlay(children : List(Pict)) : Pict = Overlay(children)

pub fn inset(all : Int, child : Pict) : Pict = Inset(all, all, all, all, child)

pub fn raw_typst(source : String) : Pict = RawTypst(source)

-- The standalone Spectra executable. Build with:
--
--   prism build packages/spectra --out ./spectra

import Cli as C

import SpectraCli (SpectraCommand, Check, Build, Clean, spectra_command)

import SpectraBuild (check_project, build_project, clean_project)

fn dispatch(command : SpectraCommand) : Int ! {FileSystem, IO, Output} =
  match command of
    Check(path) => check_project(path)
    Build(path, output, open) => build_project(path, output, open)
    Clean(path) => clean_project(path)

fn main() =
  match C.run_args(spectra_command) of
    C.Parsed(command) => exit(dispatch(command))
    C.ShowHelp(help) =>
      out_println(help)
      exit(0)
    C.BadUsage(message) =>
      eprintln(message)
      exit(2)

-- | Spectra: typed Prism presentations lowered to deterministic Typst.

import Layout as L

import Theme as Themes

import Code as SourceCode

import Example as Examples

import Example (Example, Doc)

import Backend as TypstBackend

import Backend (TypstDocument)

import Layout (Align, Left, Center, Right, Inline, Plain, Emphasis, Strong, InlineCode, Link, Colored, TextStyle, Pict, Empty, Text, CodeBlock, Image, Rectangle, Row, Column, Overlay, Inset, Fit, Fragment, RawTypst)

import Theme (Theme)

import Data.List (map, reverse, foldl, append)

import Data.Foldable (length)

import Data.String (str_join)

import Json (Json, JObj, JArr, JStr, JInt, encode)

pub type Metadata = Metadata {
  title: String,
  author: String,
  subject: String
} deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type Slide = Slide {
  title: Option(String),
  body: Pict,
  notes: List(String)
} deriving (Eq, Show)

pub type Deck = Deck {
  metadata: Metadata,
  theme: Theme,
  slides: List(Slide)
} deriving (Eq, Show)

-- The facade owns forwarding definitions for authoring values. This keeps
-- package consumers independent of internal module names during native linking;
-- users who need raw constructors can import Layout explicitly.
pub fn text(s : String) : Pict = L.text(s)

pub fn rich_text(xs : List(Inline)) : Pict = L.rich_text(xs)

pub fn link(url : String, xs : List(Inline)) : Inline = Link(url, xs)

pub fn item(s : String) : Pict = L.item(s)

pub fn row(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict = L.row(gap, children)

pub fn column(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict = L.column(gap, children)

pub fn centered(gap : Int, children : List(Pict)) : Pict = L.centered(gap, children)

pub fn inset(all : Int, child : Pict) : Pict = L.inset(all, child)

pub fn raw_typst(source : String) : Pict = L.raw_typst(source)

pub fn code_block(language : String, source : String) : Pict =
  SourceCode.code_block(language, source)

pub fn prism_code(source : String) : Pict = SourceCode.prism_code(source)

-- | Every example a reflected declaration's docstring fences, each over the
-- output the doctest runner proves it prints.
pub fn doctest(reflected : String) : Pict = Examples.doctest(reflected)

-- | A reflected declaration with its comment block removed.
pub fn definition(reflected : String) : Pict = Examples.definition(reflected)

pub fn read_doc(reflected : String) : Doc = Examples.read_doc(reflected)

pub fn examples_of(reflected : String) : List(Example) =

pub let prism_dark_theme : Theme = Themes.prism_dark_theme

pub fn pict_assets(p : Pict) : List(String) = TypstBackend.pict_assets(p)

pub fn render_pict(p : Pict, stage : Int, theme : Theme) : String =
  TypstBackend.render_pict(p, stage, theme)

pub fn render_slide_page(
  title : Option(String),
  body : Pict,
  stage : Int,
  theme : Theme
) : String =
  TypstBackend.render_slide_page(title, body, stage, theme)

pub fn typst_prelude(theme : Theme) : String = TypstBackend.typst_prelude(theme)

pub fn metadata(title : String, author : String) : Metadata =
  Metadata { title = title, author = author, subject = "" }

pub fn make_deck(meta : Metadata, theme : Theme, slides : List(Slide)) : Deck =
  Deck { metadata = meta, theme = theme, slides = slides }

pub fn title_slide(title : String, subtitle : String) : Slide =
  Slide {
    title = None,
    body = centered(18, [
        Text(TextStyle { size = 46, color = "accent", align = Center }, [
            Plain(title),
          ]),
        Text(TextStyle { size = 24, color = "muted", align = Center }, [
            Plain(subtitle),
          ]),
      ]),
    notes = Nil
  }

pub fn titled_slide(title : String, body : Pict) : Slide =
  Slide { title = Some(title), body = body, notes = Nil }

-- Builder operations are ordinary typed effects. A reveal increments the
-- logical stage attached to subsequent picts.
pub effect SlideBuilder
  place(Pict) : Unit
  reveal(Unit) : Unit

pub fn pict(p : Pict) : Unit ! {SlideBuilder} = place(p)

pub fn reveal_next() : Unit ! {SlideBuilder} = reveal(())

fn collect_slide(body : () -> Unit ! {SlideBuilder}) : List(Pict) =
  let f =
    handle body() with
      place(p) resume k =>
        \(stage, acc) -> k(())(stage, Cons(Fragment(stage, p), acc))
      reveal(_) resume k => \(stage, acc) -> k(())(stage + 1, acc)
      return _ => \(_stage, acc) -> reverse(acc)
  f(0, Nil)

pub effect DeckBuilder
  add_slide(Slide) : Unit

-- | Emit a built slide into the surrounding deck builder.
pub fn slide(
  title : String,
  body : () -> Unit ! {SlideBuilder}
) : Unit ! {DeckBuilder} =
  add_slide(titled_slide(title, Column(14, Left, collect_slide(body))))

-- | Emit a cover slide into the surrounding deck builder.
pub fn cover(title : String, subtitle : String) : Unit ! {DeckBuilder} =
  add_slide(title_slide(title, subtitle))

-- | Run the effectful authoring surface into the same pure `Deck` used by the
-- data-first API.
pub fn deck(
  meta : Metadata,
  theme : Theme,
  body : () -> Unit ! {DeckBuilder}
) : Deck =
  let f =
    handle body() with
      add_slide(s) resume k => \(acc) -> k(())(Cons(s, acc))
      return _ =>
        \(acc) -> Deck { metadata = meta, theme = theme, slides = reverse(acc) }
  f(Nil)

fn pages_for_slide(slide : Slide) : Int = 1 + max_stage(slide.body)

fn page_count(slides : List(Slide)) : Int =
  foldl(\(n, slide) -> n + pages_for_slide(slide), 0, slides)

fn stages_for(slide : Slide, stage : Int, theme : Theme) : List(String) =
  let page = render_slide_page(slide.title, slide.body, stage, theme)
  if stage >= max_stage(slide.body) then
    [page]
  else
    Cons(page, stages_for(slide, stage + 1, theme))

fn render_slides(slides : List(Slide), theme : Theme) : List(String) =
  match slides of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(slide, rest) =>
      append(stages_for(slide, 0, theme), render_slides(rest, theme))

fn deck_assets(slides : List(Slide)) : List(String) =
  match slides of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(slide, rest) => append(pict_assets(slide.body), deck_assets(rest))

-- | Pure, deterministic Typst lowering. Logical slides with reveals expand to
-- one physical PDF page per stage.
pub fn render_typst(d : Deck) : TypstDocument =
  let pages = render_slides(d.slides, d.theme)
  TypstDocument {
    format = "spectra-typst-document-v1",
    source = concat(
        typst_prelude(d.theme),
        concat(str_join("\n#pagebreak()\n", pages), "\n"),
      ),
    logical_slides = length(d.slides),
    physical_pages = page_count(d.slides),
    assets = deck_assets(d.slides)
  }

-- | The exact one-line envelope consumed by the `spectra` host frontend.
pub fn envelope(d : Deck) : String =
  let doc = render_typst(d)
  encode(JObj([
      ("format", JStr("spectra-envelope-v1")),
      ("document_format", JStr(doc.format)),
      ("source", JStr(doc.source)),
      ("logical_slides", JInt(doc.logical_slides)),
      ("physical_pages", JInt(doc.physical_pages)),
      ("theme", JStr(d.theme.name)),
      ("title", JStr(d.metadata.title)),
      ("author", JStr(d.metadata.author)),
      ("assets", JArr(map(\(asset) -> JStr(asset), doc.assets))),
    ]))

-- | Emit exactly one framed envelope. The host rejects any extra output, so a
-- stray debug print can never be interpreted as Typst source.
pub fn emit_deck(d : Deck) : Unit = println(concat("SPECTRA/1 ", envelope(d)))

-- | Standalone Spectra build orchestration, written in Prism.
--
-- The executable treats `prism` and `typst` as explicit external tools. Deck
-- construction and Typst lowering remain pure package code; this module is the
-- narrow host shell that captures the framed envelope and writes artifacts.

import Data.String (contains, ends_with, starts_with, str_of_char, trim)

import Data.Result (map_err)

import Json (Json, JObj, JStr, JInt, decode, encode, json_error_message)

pub type DeckEnvelope = DeckEnvelope {
  source: String,
  logical_slides: Int,
  physical_pages: Int,
  title: String
} deriving (Eq, Show)

let envelope_prefix : String = "SPECTRA/1 "

fn quote_body(value : String, i : Int, acc : String) : String =
  if i >= str_len(value) then
    acc
  elif char_at(value, i) == 39 then
    quote_body(value, i + 1, "{acc}'\\''")
  else
    quote_body(value, i + 1, "{acc}{str_of_char(chr(char_at(value, i)))}")

-- | Quote one opaque argument for the POSIX shell used by `system`.
pub fn shell_quote(value : String) : String = "'{quote_body(value, 0, "")}'"

fn join_path(root : String, rest : String) : String =
  if ends_with("/", root) then
    "{root}{rest}"
  else
    "{root}/{rest}"

fn field(name : String, fields : List((String, Json))) : Option(Json) =
  match fields of
    Nil => None
    Cons((key, value), rest) =>
      if key == name then
        Some(value)
      else
        field(name, rest)

fn string_field(
  name : String,
  fields : List((String, Json))
) : Result(String, String) =
  match field(name, fields) of
    Some(JStr(value)) => Ok(value)
    _ => Err("deck envelope field '{name}' must be a string")

fn int_field(
  name : String,
  fields : List((String, Json))
) : Result(Int, String) =
  match field(name, fields) of
    Some(JInt(value)) => Ok(value)
    _ => Err("deck envelope field '{name}' must be an integer")

fn envelope_fields(fields : List((String, Json))) : Result(DeckEnvelope, String) =
  let format = string_field("format", fields)?
  let document_format = string_field("document_format", fields)?
  let source = string_field("source", fields)?
  let logical = int_field("logical_slides", fields)?
  let physical = int_field("physical_pages", fields)?
  let title = string_field("title", fields)?
  if format /= "spectra-envelope-v1" then
    Err("unsupported deck envelope '{format}'")
  elif document_format /= "spectra-typst-document-v1" then
    Err("unsupported Typst document envelope '{document_format}'")
  elif logical <= 0 || physical < logical then
    Err("invalid logical/physical page counts")
  else
    Ok(
        DeckEnvelope {
          source = source,
          logical_slides = logical,
          physical_pages = physical,
          title = title
        },
      )

pub fn parse_envelope(stdout : String) : Result((DeckEnvelope, String), String) =
  let framed = trim(stdout)
  if not(starts_with(envelope_prefix, framed)) then
    Err("expected one 'SPECTRA/1 ' envelope; does main call Spectra.emit_deck?")
  else
    let body = substring(
        framed,
        str_len(envelope_prefix),
        str_len(framed) - str_len(envelope_prefix),
      )
    let decoded = map_err(
        \(err) -> "invalid deck envelope JSON: {json_error_message(err)}",
        decode(body),
      )?
    match decoded of
      JObj(fields) =>
        let envelope = envelope_fields(fields)?
        Ok((envelope, encode(JObj(fields))))
      _ => Err("deck envelope must be a JSON object")

fn run(label : String, command : String) : Result(Unit, String) ! {IO} =
  let status = system(command)
  if status == 0 then
    Ok(())
  else
    Err("{label} failed with exit status {status}")

fn safe_output(name : String) : Bool =
  name /= ""
    && ends_with(".pdf", name)
    && not(contains("/", name))
    && not(contains("\\", name))
    && name /= ".pdf"

fn write_text(path : String, body : String) : Result(Unit, String) ! {IO} =
  map_err(
      \(message) -> "cannot write {path}: {message}",
      write_file(path, body),
    )

-- | Prove the examples the deck shows. A slide renders a `prism` fence beside
-- the `output` fence written under it; this hands both to the compiler's
-- doctest runner, which compiles the example and compares what it actually
-- prints. An example that has drifted from its output fails the build rather
-- than reaching a screen.
fn doctest_steps(project : String) : Result(Unit, String) ! {IO} =
  run("deck doctests", "prism docs {shell_quote(project)} --test")

fn check_steps(project : String) : Result(Unit, String) ! {IO} =
  run("Prism check", "prism check {shell_quote(project)}")?
  doctest_steps(project)?
  run("Typst discovery", "typst --version")?
  Ok(())

pub fn check_project(project : String) : Int ! {IO, Output} =
  match check_steps(project) of
    Ok(_) =>
      out_println("Spectra project is ready")
      0
    Err(message) =>
      eprintln("spectra: {message}")
      1

fn build_steps(
  project : String,
  output : String
) : Result((DeckEnvelope, String), String) ! {FileSystem, IO} =
  let target = join_path(project, "target/spectra")
  let evaluator = join_path(target, "deck-evaluator")
  let captured = join_path(target, "deck.stdout")
  let deck_path = join_path(target, "deck.deck.json")
  let typst_path = join_path(target, "deck.typ")
  let pdf_path = join_path(target, output)
  run("creating target/spectra", "mkdir -p -- {shell_quote(target)}")?
  doctest_steps(project)?
  run(
      "deck compilation",
      "prism build {shell_quote(project)} --out {shell_quote(evaluator)}",
    )?
  run("deck evaluation", "{shell_quote(evaluator)} > {shell_quote(captured)}")?
  let parsed = parse_envelope(read_file(captured))?
  let (envelope, envelope_json) = parsed
  write_text(deck_path, "{envelope_json}\n")?
  write_text(typst_path, envelope.source)?
  run(
      "Typst compilation (generated source retained at {typst_path})",
      "typst compile {shell_quote(typst_path)} {shell_quote(pdf_path)}",
    )?
  Ok((envelope, pdf_path))

pub fn build_project(
  project : String,
  output : String,
  open : Bool
) : Int ! {FileSystem, IO, Output} =
  if not(safe_output(output)) then
    eprintln("spectra: --output must be a plain relative .pdf filename")
    2
  else
    match build_steps(project, output) of
      Err(message) =>
        eprintln("spectra: {message}")
        1
      Ok((envelope, pdf_path)) =>
        out_println(
            "built {pdf_path} ({envelope.logical_slides} logical slides, {envelope.physical_pages} physical pages)",
          )
        if open then
          let _opened = system(
              "open {shell_quote(pdf_path)} 2>/dev/null || xdg-open {shell_quote(pdf_path)}",
            )
          ()
        0

pub fn clean_project(project : String) : Int ! {IO} =
  if project == "" || project == "/" then
    eprintln("spectra: refusing unsafe project path")
    2
  else
    let target = join_path(project, "target/spectra")
    match run("clean", "rm -rf -- {shell_quote(target)}") of
      Ok(_) => 0
      Err(message) =>
        eprintln("spectra: {message}")
        1

test fn shell_arguments_are_single_quoted() =
  if shell_quote("a'b c") == "'a'\\''b c'" then
    ()
  else
    fail()

test fn framed_envelope_rejects_plain_output() =
  match parse_envelope("debug output") of
    Err(_) => ()
    Ok(_) => fail()

-- | Spectra's command grammar, built applicatively with Std `Cli`.

import Cli as C

import Cli (Command, Group, SubCmd)

pub type SpectraCommand
  = Check(String)
  | Build(String, String, Bool)
  | Clean(String)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

fn path_parser() =
  C.arg_str_default(
      "PATH",
      "project directory (default: current directory)",
      ".",
    )

fn check_parser() = C.map_p(\(path) -> Check(path), path_parser())

fn clean_parser() = C.map_p(\(path) -> Clean(path), path_parser())

fn build_parser() =
  C.build3(
      \(path) -> \(output) -> \(open) -> Build(path, output, open),
      path_parser(),
      C.opt_str("output", "o", "PDF", "output PDF name", "deck.pdf"),
      C.switch("open", "", "open the resulting PDF"),
    )

pub let spectra_command : C.Command(SpectraCommand) =
  Command {
    name = "spectra",
    about = "build typed Prism presentations through Typst",
    body = Group([
        SubCmd {
          key = "check",
          about = "check a deck and required tools",
          sub = check_parser()
        },
        SubCmd {
          key = "build",
          about = "build inspectable Typst and a PDF",
          sub = build_parser()
        },
        SubCmd {
          key = "clean",
          about = "remove only target/spectra",
          sub = clean_parser()
        },
      ])
  }

pub fn parse_spectra_argv(argv : List(String)) : C.Outcome(SpectraCommand) =
  C.run_argv(spectra_command, argv)

test fn default_paths_are_current_directory() =
  match parse_spectra_argv(["check"]) of
    C.Parsed(Check(path)) =>
      if path == "." then
        ()
      else
        fail()
    _ => fail()

test fn build_combines_path_output_and_open_applicatively() =
  match (parse_spectra_argv(["build", "talk", "--output", "talk.pdf", "--open"])) of
    C.Parsed(Build(path, output, open)) =>
      if path == "talk" && output == "talk.pdf" && open then
        ()
      else
        fail()
    _ => fail()

test fn extra_paths_are_rejected() =
  match parse_spectra_argv(["clean", "one", "two"]) of
    C.BadUsage(_) => ()
    _ => fail()

type TypstDocument = TypstDocument {
  format: String,
  source: String,
  logical_slides: Int,
  physical_pages: Int,
  assets: List(String)

fn color(name : String, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  let value =
    if name == "" then
      theme.foreground
    elif name == "accent" then
      theme.accent
    elif name == "muted" then
      theme.muted
    else
      name
  T.call("rgb", [T.string("#{value}")])

defs.name: alignment
defs.source:
fn alignment(align : Align) : T.Doc =
  match align of
    Left => T.atom("left")
    Center => T.atom("center")
    Right => T.atom("right")

defs.name: inline_doc
defs.source:
fn inline_doc(x : Inline, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match x of
    Plain(s) => T.call("text", [T.string(s)])
    InlineCode(s) =>
      T.call("raw", [T.string(s), T.named("lang", T.string("prism"))])
    Emphasis(xs) => T.content_call("emph", Nil, inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Strong(xs) => T.content_call("strong", Nil, inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Link(url, xs) =>
      T.content_call("link", [T.string(url)], inline_docs(xs, theme))
    Colored(name, xs) =>
      T.content_call(
          "text",
          [T.named("fill", color(name, theme))],
          inline_docs(xs, theme),
        )

defs.name: inline_docs
defs.source:
fn inline_docs(xs : List(Inline), theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match xs of
    Nil => T.empty()
    Cons(x, Nil) => inline_doc(x, theme)
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      T.concat_docs([
          inline_doc(x, theme),
          T.atom(" + "),
          inline_docs(rest, theme),
        ])

fn max2(a : Int, b : Int) : Int =
  if a > b then
    a
  else
    b

defs.name: max_stage_list
defs.source:
fn max_stage_list(xs : List(Pict)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(p, rest) => max2(max_stage(p), max_stage_list(rest))

defs.name: max_stage
defs.source:
fn max_stage(p : Pict) : Int =
  match p of
    Empty => 0
    Text(_, _) => 0
    CodeBlock(_, _) => 0
    Image(_) => 0
    Rectangle(_, _, _) => 0
    Row(_, xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Column(_, _, xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Overlay(xs) => max_stage_list(xs)
    Inset(_, _, _, _, child) => max_stage(child)
    Fit(_, child) => max_stage(child)
    Fragment(stage, child) => max2(stage, max_stage(child))
    RawTypst(_) => 0

fn assets_list(xs : List(Pict)) : List(String) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(p, rest) => append(pict_assets(p), assets_list(rest))

defs.name: pict_assets
defs.source:
fn pict_assets(p : Pict) : List(String) =
  match p of
    Empty => Nil
    Text(_, _) => Nil
    CodeBlock(_, _) => Nil
    Image(path) => [path]
    Rectangle(_, _, _) => Nil
    Row(_, xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Column(_, _, xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Overlay(xs) => assets_list(xs)
    Inset(_, _, _, _, child) => pict_assets(child)
    Fit(_, child) => pict_assets(child)
    Fragment(_, child) => pict_assets(child)
    RawTypst(_) => Nil

fn pict_docs(xs : List(Pict), stage : Int, theme : Theme) : List(T.Doc) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(p, rest) =>
      Cons(pict_doc(p, stage, theme), pict_docs(rest, stage, theme))

defs.name: pict_doc
defs.source:
fn pict_doc(p : Pict, stage : Int, theme : Theme) : T.Doc =
  match p of
    Empty => T.atom("none")
    Text(style, xs) =>
      let size =
        if style.size <= 0 then
          theme.body_size
        else
          style.size
      T.call("align", [
          alignment(style.align),
          T.content_call(
              "text",
              [
                  T.named("size", T.pt(size)),
                  T.named("fill", color(style.color, theme)),
                ],
              inline_docs(xs, theme),
            ),
        ])
    CodeBlock(language, source) =>
      T.content_call("block", [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("fill", color(theme.code_background, theme)), T.named("inset", T.pt(14)), T.named("radius", T.pt(7))], T.content_call("text", [T.named("fill", color(theme.code_foreground, theme)), T.named("font", T.string(theme.code_font)), T.named("size", T.pt(theme.code_size))], T.call("raw", [
          T.string(source),
          T.named("block", T.atom("true")),
          T.named("lang", T.string(language)),
        ])))
    Image(path) =>
      T.call("image", [
          T.string(path),
          T.named("width", T.percent(100)),
          T.named("height", T.percent(100)),
          T.named("fit", T.string("contain")),
        ])
    Rectangle(name, width, height) =>
      T.call("rect", [
          T.named("width", T.pt(width)),
          T.named("height", T.pt(height)),
          T.named("fill", color(name, theme)),
        ])
    Row(gap, children) =>
      T.call(
          "stack",
          Cons(
              T.named("dir", T.atom("ltr")),
              Cons(
                  T.named("spacing", T.pt(gap)),
                  pict_docs(children, stage, theme),
                ),
            ),
        )
    Column(gap, align, children) =>
      T.call("align", [
          alignment(align),
          T.call(
              "stack",
              Cons(
                  T.named("dir", T.atom("ttb")),
                  Cons(
                      T.named("spacing", T.pt(gap)),
                      pict_docs(children, stage, theme),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        ])
    Overlay(children) =>
      T.content_call(
          "block",
          [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("height", T.percent(100))],
          T.call("stack", pict_docs(children, stage, theme)),
        )
    Inset(top, right, bottom, left, child) =>
      T.content_call(
          "block",
          [
              T.named("inset", T.tuple([
                  T.named("top", T.pt(top)),
                  T.named("right", T.pt(right)),
                  T.named("bottom", T.pt(bottom)),
                  T.named("left", T.pt(left)),
                ])),
            ],
          pict_doc(child, stage, theme),
        )
    Fit(_, child) =>
      T.content_call(
          "box",
          [T.named("width", T.percent(100)), T.named("height", T.percent(100))],
          pict_doc(child, stage, theme),
        )
    Fragment(at, child) =>
      if at <= stage then
        pict_doc(child, stage, theme)
      else
        T.atom("none")
    RawTypst(source) => T.raw(source)

  doc : List(String)

defs.name: after_code
defs.source:
fn after_code(
  rest : List(String),
  prose : List(String),
  acc : List(Example)
) : (List(String), List(Example)) =
  match rest of
    Cons(next, tail) =>
      if starts_with(output_fence, next) then
        walk(tail, InOutput, Nil, prose, acc)
      else
        walk(rest, InProse, Nil, prose, acc)
    Nil => (reverse(prose), reverse(acc))

defs.name: walk
defs.source:
fn walk(
  lines : List(String),
  region : Region,
  buf : List(String),
  prose : List(String),
  acc : List(Example)
) : (List(String), List(Example)) =
  match lines of
    Nil => (reverse(prose), reverse(acc))
    Cons(line, rest) =>
      match region of
        InProse =>
          match region_of(line) of
            Some(next) => walk(rest, next, Nil, prose, acc)
            None => walk(rest, InProse, Nil, Cons(line, prose), acc)
        InCode =>
          if closes(line) then
            after_code(
                rest,
                prose,
                Cons(
                    Example { code = lines_of(reverse(buf)), output = "" },
                    acc,
                  ),
              )
          elif hidden(line) then
            walk(rest, InCode, buf, prose, acc)
          else
            walk(rest, InCode, Cons(line, buf), prose, acc)
        InOutput =>
          if closes(line) then
            walk(
                rest,
                InProse,
                Nil,
                prose,
                with_output(lines_of(reverse(buf)), acc),
              )
          else
            walk(rest, InOutput, Cons(line, buf), prose, acc)
        InOther =>
          if closes(line) then
            walk(rest, InProse, Nil, prose, acc)
          else
            walk(rest, InOther, buf, prose, acc)

fn quote_body(value : String, i : Int, acc : String) : String =
  if i >= str_len(value) then
    acc
  elif char_at(value, i) == 39 then
    quote_body(value, i + 1, "{acc}'\\''")
  else
    quote_body(value, i + 1, "{acc}{str_of_char(chr(char_at(value, i)))}")

defs.name: envelope_fields
defs.source:
fn envelope_fields(fields : List((String, Json))) : Result(DeckEnvelope, String) =
  let format = string_field("format", fields)?
  let document_format = string_field("document_format", fields)?
  let source = string_field("source", fields)?
  let logical = int_field("logical_slides", fields)?
  let physical = int_field("physical_pages", fields)?
  let title = string_field("title", fields)?
  if format /= "spectra-envelope-v1" then
    Err("unsupported deck envelope '{format}'")
  elif document_format /= "spectra-typst-document-v1" then
    Err("unsupported Typst document envelope '{document_format}'")
  elif logical <= 0 || physical < logical then
    Err("invalid logical/physical page counts")
  else
    Ok(
        DeckEnvelope {
          source = source,
          logical_slides = logical,
          physical_pages = physical,
          title = title
        },
      )

defs.source:
fn build_project(
  project : String,
  output : String,
  open : Bool
) : Int ! {FileSystem, IO, Output} =
  if not(safe_output(output)) then
    eprintln("spectra: --output must be a plain relative .pdf filename")
    2
  else
    match build_steps(project, output) of
      Err(message) =>
        eprintln("spectra: {message}")
        1
      Ok((envelope, pdf_path)) =>
        out_println(
            "built {pdf_path} ({envelope.logical_slides} logical slides, {envelope.physical_pages} physical pages)",
          )
        if open then
          let _opened = system(
              "open {shell_quote(pdf_path)} 2>/dev/null || xdg-open {shell_quote(pdf_path)}",
            )
          ()
        0

defs.name: clean_project
defs.source:
fn clean_project(project : String) : Int ! {IO} =
  if project == "" || project == "/" then
    eprintln("spectra: refusing unsafe project path")
    2
  else
    let target = join_path(project, "target/spectra")
    match run("clean", "rm -rf -- {shell_quote(target)}") of
      Ok(_) => 0
      Err(message) =>
        eprintln("spectra: {message}")
        1
